outputs.L1: A profile comparator for comparing a human operator with a clone, the profile comparator comprising a storage device, a simulation processor, and a parameter comparator. The storage device includes a recording of at least one parameter during an activity session of a platform, the platform including at least one control system. The at least one parameter comprises at least one of a parameter of the platform and an action performed by an operator of the platform during the activity session. The storage device further includes a predetermined profile. The simulation processor is configured to generate a virtual clone of the platform according to at least one recorded parameter and to manage the virtual clone according to the predetermined profile. The parameter comparator is configured to compare at least one comparison parameter with a corresponding comparison parameter of the virtual clone and to determine at least one deviation in which the comparison parameter deviates from the corresponding comparison parameter of the virtual clone.
outputs.L2: A profile comparison system for evaluating differences between a human operator and a clone comprises a storage device, a simulation processor, and a parameter comparator. The storage device contains a predetermined profile and a record of at least one parameter captured during an activity session involving a platform with at least one control system. The recorded parameter represents either a platform parameter, an action performed by the platform operator during the session, or both. Based on at least one recorded parameter, the simulation processor creates a virtual clone of the platform and operates that clone in accordance with the predetermined profile. The parameter comparator compares at least one comparison parameter with the corresponding parameter of the virtual clone and identifies at least one instance in which the comparison parameter differs from that of the virtual clone.
outputs.L3:
The profile comparator evaluates the performance of a human operator against that of a virtual clone. During an activity session, a storage device records at least one parameter associated with the platform or at least one action performed by the operator. The storage device also maintains a predetermined operating profile.

Using one or more of the recorded parameters, a simulation processor generates a virtual clone of the platform. The processor then operates the virtual clone in accordance with the predetermined profile, thereby creating a simulated reference performance.

A parameter comparator compares the parameters recorded during the actual activity session with the corresponding parameters produced by the virtual clone. Based on this comparison, the comparator identifies deviations between the human operator’s performance and the performance represented by the predetermined profile.
outputs.L4:
A profile comparator provides a systematic way to evaluate the performance or behavior of a human operator by comparing the operator with a virtual clone operating under equivalent conditions. The comparator may be used with a vehicle, machine, control system, simulator, or other platform whose operation can be represented by measurable parameters and reproduced in a simulation environment.

During operation, the system records relevant platform and operator parameters. Platform parameters may include speed, position, acceleration, orientation, environmental conditions, system status, control responses, or equipment configuration. Operator parameters may include control inputs, reaction times, decisions, task sequences, workload indicators, or other measurable actions. The recorded information can be synchronized and stored as a time-based operational profile.

A simulation of the platform is then executed using the recorded conditions or corresponding scenario data. Within the simulation, a virtual clone performs the same or a comparable task. The clone is managed according to a predetermined profile that defines expected, preferred, typical, or reference behavior. This profile may be based on established operating procedures, expert performance, historical data, training requirements, safety limits, or a model tailored to the individual operator.

The profile comparator selects parameters that are suitable for direct comparison between the human operator and the virtual clone. It evaluates differences in values, timing, sequence, frequency, and response to particular events. For example, the system may determine whether the operator reacted later than the clone, applied excessive or insufficient control input, departed from an expected operating path, or used a different decision-making sequence.

Identified deviations may be quantified according to their magnitude, duration, frequency, or operational significance. The system can apply thresholds or weighting factors so that minor variations are distinguished from deviations that affect safety, efficiency, accuracy, or mission success. The resulting comparison may be presented as a score, report, timeline, graphical display, alert, or set of recommended corrective actions.

By comparing actual human behavior with the controlled behavior of the virtual clone, the system enables objective assessment of operator performance. The results may support training, certification, performance monitoring, procedure validation, accident analysis, or human-factors research. Repeated comparisons can also reveal trends over time, allowing the predetermined clone profile or the operator’s training program to be adjusted as operational requirements change.
outputs.L5:
# A Profile Comparator

A profile comparator, also known as an optical comparator or profile projector, is a precision measuring instrument used to inspect the shape, dimensions, and surface features of manufactured components. It magnifies the silhouette of a part and projects it onto a screen, allowing an operator to compare the component with a drawing, template, or digital reference.

The device works by placing a component on an illuminated stage. Light creates an enlarged image of the part’s profile, which is projected onto a calibrated screen. Linear dimensions, angles, radii, threads, and complex contours can then be measured without direct contact. This makes the instrument particularly useful for inspecting small, delicate, or easily deformed parts.

Profile comparators are widely used in manufacturing, quality control, automotive production, aerospace engineering, and toolmaking. Typical applications include checking gears, cutting tools, screws, stamped components, and machined parts. Modern digital systems may include automated edge detection, coordinate measurement, data storage, and software-based comparison with CAD models.

The main advantages of a profile comparator are its accuracy, ease of use, and non-contact measuring capability. However, reliable results depend on correct calibration, suitable magnification, careful alignment, and proper part positioning. When used correctly, a profile comparator provides an efficient way to verify that components meet specified dimensional and geometric tolerances.

A profile comparison system comprising: storage configured to store recorded parameters representing operation of an operator, a platform, or both; a simulation processor configured to generate a simulated clone of the operator, the platform, or both and to produce simulated parameters corresponding to the recorded parameters; and a parameter comparator configured to compare the recorded parameters with the simulated parameters and generate an indication of a deviation satisfying a deviation criterion.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Formulate a single claim for technology that records a vehicle or platform activity session, creates a virtual clone from the recorded data, runs it using a predefined operator profile, and compares the resulting parameters.
counterfactuals.output: 1. A computer-implemented method comprising: recording, by one or more sensors, data representing an activity session performed by a vehicle or mobile platform; generating, by one or more processors based on the recorded data, a virtual clone that simulates the vehicle or mobile platform and conditions associated with the activity session; executing the virtual clone according to a predefined operator profile to produce simulated session parameters; and comparing the simulated session parameters with corresponding parameters derived from the recorded activity session to generate comparison data indicative of differences between operation under the predefined operator profile and operation during the recorded activity session.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, a system for evaluating a human operator against a simulated clone by comparing operator actions or platform parameters and identifying deviations.
counterfactuals.output:
A system for evaluating performance of a human operator relative to a simulated operator clone, the system comprising: one or more processors; a data acquisition interface configured to receive operator data representative of actions performed by the human operator and/or parameters of a platform controlled by the human operator; and a simulation engine configured to instantiate the simulated operator clone based at least in part on a behavioral model associated with the human operator, and to generate reference data representative of actions predicted to be performed by the simulated operator clone and/or corresponding simulated platform parameters under operating conditions corresponding to those experienced by the human operator.

The one or more processors are configured to temporally and contextually align the operator data with the reference data, determine one or more deviations between respective operator actions, platform parameters, or combinations thereof, and evaluate the one or more deviations according to at least one predetermined or adaptively determined criterion. The system is further configured to generate an evaluation output identifying each deviation that satisfies a threshold condition, the evaluation output optionally including a deviation magnitude, deviation type, temporal location, operational context, probable cause, and/or performance score.

In certain embodiments, the behavioral model is generated or updated using historical operator data, training-session data, physiological data, platform-state data, environmental data, or combinations thereof. The simulated operator clone may be executed concurrently with operation of the platform, retrospectively using recorded data, or prospectively in a predictive simulation. The evaluation output may be provided to a display, training system, supervisory system, safety system, or platform controller for operator feedback, certification, remediation, anomaly detection, or adaptive control.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
